claims.text: Controlled heat treatment can promote short-range chemical ordering.
Heat-treatment-induced short-range ordering produces Cr-rich nanoclusters or precipitates.
The Cr-rich nanoclusters produced by heat treatment occur near the steel surface.
Short-range ordering causes chromium atoms to segregate toward the surface.
Elevated near-surface chromium facilitates formation and stability of a robust chromium oxide passive film.
The chromium oxide passive film resists corrosive attack.
Stainless steels lacking induced ordering retain a more homogeneous chromium distribution.
A more homogeneous chromium distribution produces less effective passivation than the proposed ordered state.
Heat-treated steels with confirmed ordering and near-surface chromium enrichment will have lower corrosion rates than untreated steels.
Heat-treated steels with confirmed ordering and near-surface chromium enrichment will maintain passive-layer stability longer than untreated steels.
Untreated homogenized steels will have higher corrosion rates and less durable passive films under otherwise identical conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies to stainless steels containing approximately 12–20% chromium.
The mechanism should operate across stainless steels with similar bulk chromium contents in chemical-processing and nuclear-power environments.
The mechanism may fail for substantially different alloy compositions or under extremely oxidizing conditions.
A 3.5% NaCl solution is a suitable controlled environment for potentiodynamic corrosion testing.
Potentiodynamic testing can assess corrosion behavior in saline solution.
Treated and untreated samples of identical chemical composition should be compared under identical corrosion conditions.
Failure to observe lower corrosion, stronger passive-film formation, and corresponding near-surface chromium enrichment in treated samples would falsify the hypothesis.
The degree of short-range order required to optimize chromium segregation is not yet quantitatively known.
The quantitative improvement in corrosion resistance remains to be determined experimentally.

contradictions.description: The control state is described as both 'as-cast' and 'homogenized.' Homogenization normally entails a post-casting heat treatment, so the processing history is internally ambiguous unless 'homogenized' is being used only to describe compositional uniformity.
